description:
Creates a NEW TabTree board (whiteboard): shapes (rect, ellipse, diamond, text, sticky), TABLES (kind "table" with `cells` — a comparison, a pricing grid, a RACI), IMAGES (kind "image" with a `file` path — your logos, photos, posters, placed where you say) and arrow connections that stay anchored to the shapes in the app. With no x/y coordinates, layout is automatic by level (the connections define the hierarchy, left to right). Good for a diagram, a flow, a brainstorm. In a flowchart use ellipse for start/end, rect for a step, and diamond for a decision — its text should read as a closed question with exactly two ways out.

FIT THE TEXT TO THE BOX. A box shows roughly (w−24)/7 characters per line and (h−10)/20 lines, and every blank line costs a full line. Write captions, not paragraphs: when filling a canvas template (Business Model Canvas, Lean Canvas, SWOT…), the shipped templates use 70–110 characters per block, and that is what looks composed. Longer text is shrunk to fit — nothing ever spills out — but past ~11px it stops being readable and the response will warn you.

a0.description: arc only — start angle in degrees, 0 at 12 o'clock, clockwise

a1.description: arc only — end angle in degrees (a1 > a0; a full circle is a0=0, a1=360)

cell.description: Puts THIS element INSIDE a table cell: the id of a table element, then the 0-based row and column (row 0 is the header row). Use it for a LOGO next to its name (an image), a big title (kind "text" with size 24-40) or a coloured badge (a shape). The app stacks it under the cell's text, centred, shrinks a wide image to the column width, and grows the row to fit; it moves with the table. x/y are ignored. Not for a table or a sticky note.

cells.description: table only — the rows, each a list of cell texts, e.g. [["Plan","Price"],["Free","$0"],["Pro","$12"]]. Up to 80 rows × 20 columns, 2000 characters a cell; shorter rows are padded.

color.description: Hex fill colour (shapes) or sticky-note colour

cw.description: table only — relative column widths, one positive number per column (e.g. [2,1,1]); even by default

data.description: image only — a data:image/(png|jpeg|webp|gif|svg+xml) URL instead of a file

file.description: image only — full path of a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/SVG file on this machine. Rasters are re-encoded to about 840 px; an SVG is kept as is (300 KB max).

header.description: table only — false when the first row is data, not a header (default true)

id.description: Logical id used by connections (defaults to the index)

ir.description: arc only — inner-radius fraction 0..0.9 (0 = pie slice, 0.55 = donut)

kind.description: Type (defaults to rect). table = a GRID of text — give `cells` (rows of cell texts; the first row is the header unless header:false); it is sized by its columns (140 px each unless w is given) and grows with its text; `text` is ignored, `color` colours the header row. Put a logo or a big title INSIDE a cell with `cell` on that image or text element (e.g. a competitor table: the brand logo in column 0 of each row); make rows taller with `rowHeights`, centre the text with valign "middle". image = a PICTURE placed freely on the board — a logo, a photo, a poster: give `file` (full path of a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/SVG on this machine) or `data` (a data:image/… URL); w/h keep the image's proportions when only one (or neither, 220 px on the long side) is given; arrows can start or end on it; `text` is ignored. diamond = a decision in a flowchart, trap = a pyramid/funnel tier (tk = small-side ratio, negative when the base is the narrow side), chev = a process step pointing forward, arc = a pie slice (a0/a1 in degrees from 12 o'clock, ir = inner-radius fraction for a donut).

pic.description: Optional picture drawn INSIDE the element, no file needed — "a:<id>" for a built-in illustration (roles: manager, client, expert, assistant, coach, learner, developer, seller, support, speaker, freelancer, group — plus person, team, idea, target, rocket…) or "e:<emoji>". Not on arc/trap/chev.

rowHeights.description: table only — a MINIMUM height per row in px (0 = fit the text), e.g. [0, 110, 110] for taller rows that hold logos. A row still grows when its content needs more room.

tk.description: trap only — small-side/large-side ratio, 0..0.95 (0 = triangle); NEGATIVE puts the narrow side at the bottom (funnel tier)

valign.description: table only — vertical alignment of the cell text: "top" (default), "middle" or "bottom" for the whole table, or rows of those words (one list per row).

z.description: Stacking order, -9..9 (default 0). At equal z the app paints images UNDER shapes, shapes under sticky notes — so a filled background panel hides a logo placed on it. Give such a panel z:-1 (or the image z:1) to keep the picture visible.

folder.description: Optional TabTree folder. A NAME or a full PATH ("Ai4X / Programmes"). When several folders share a name, the shallowest is used and the answer says which.

space.description: Optional TabTree SPACE to put it in, by name — one of the user's spaces, or a TEAM space they are an editor of (every member then sees it). list_maps shows the spaces. Omit for the user's own library.

style.description: Optional look of the document. Omit it for the default.

background.description: Page background: dots (default), plain, grid, graph paper, ruled lines, isometric, paper, cream, kraft, aged, mist, sage, dawn, blueprint, slate (dark), chalkboard (dark).

font.description: Type family: grotesk (corporate), humanist (warm), condensed (dense), rounded (friendly), serif/garamond (editorial), didone (elegant), slab (sturdy), typewriter, mono (technical), hand (handwritten).

shape.description: Node shape: cards (default), line = underlined, plain = plain text.

skin.description: Structural skin — borders, shadows, corners: classic (default), soft (borderless, rounded), flat (no shadows — for print), paper (soft warm shadows), ink (fine ink outline), draft (square corners, technical), sticker (white cut-out ring), brutal (thick ink borders, hard shadows), arcade (square, hard short shadows). Travels with the board and into exported images.

name: create_board
